## CRI MXFP MoE integration: hardware validation, model performance and accuracy controls

### Summary

- Native ARK CRI kernels were built successfully and exercised through vLLM.
- MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights passed real-device kernel/model smoke tests
  and now also have a complete 48-layer model evaluation.
- MXFP8, normal MXFP4 and FWHT+MXFP4 use the same complete 48-layer
  Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP4 checkpoint, with an independent INT4 W4A16 accuracy reference.
- All four complete-model configurations produced coherent English/Chinese responses.
- The MXFP8-activation control measured PPL **13.680705** and GSM8K **24/32
  (75.000%)** on the fixed subsets. It was slower than normal MXFP4 in every
  timed case; decode-heavy batch latency was **9.71–13.27×** normal MXFP4.
- **No model-level FWHT speedup was demonstrated:** prefill-heavy cases were
  approximately tied; decode-heavy cases had 1.48–3.29% higher latency.
- Quantitative accuracy results in this comment cover the INT4 W4A16 reference,
  normal MXFP4 baseline, MXFP8-activation control and FWHT+MXFP4 configuration.
  These are preliminary subset results; no accuracy-equivalence claim is made.
- Performance results shown here cover only MXFP8, normal MXFP4 and FWHT+MXFP4;
  INT4 W4A16 is retained only as an accuracy reference.

### 1. Environment and implementation

| Item | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Linux, Docker container `moe` |
| Device | Intel CRI, reported as Intel Graphics `0x674F`, 121.59 GiB |
| Full-model comparison | Physical GPU 6 only, exposed as logical device 0 |
| Earlier native-kernel/smoke tests | Physical GPU 7 only, separate from GPU 6 comparisons |
| Device isolation | `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6`, `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu` for the comparison |
| PyTorch | Custom CRI `2.14.0a0+gitd35bb04` |
| Triton | `3.8.0+git2f96b0eb` |
| DPC++ | 2026.2.0 |
| vLLM XPU kernels | `0.1.15.4` |
| vLLM integration branch | `feat/cri-mxfp4-moe`, based on `zhenzhong/w4a8_moe` |
| AutoRound integration branch | `feat/cri-mxfp4-moe-integration`, based on `feat/mxfp8-mxfp4-moe-bdpas` |

The tested source snapshots include uncommitted integration changes; the base
branch HEADs are not immutable identifiers for the complete tested patch.
The existing custom CRI PyTorch/Triton wheels were preserved.

The full ARK XPU extension compiled and linked successfully (289 build steps).
Runtime capability checks confirmed `sycl_target=cri` and `has_mxfp_bdpas=True`.
Compatible external CRI block-scaled headers were used only for the BDPAS
translation unit; the pinned SYCL-TLA headers were retained for ordinary kernels.

| Mode | Selector | Routed-expert computation | Coverage reported here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MXFP8 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp8` | Dynamic group-32 E4M3 activations × E2M1 weights | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, performance, E2E; native tests and earlier 12-layer smoke |
| Normal MXFP4 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp4` | Raw activations quantized to MXFP4, without FWHT; original packed weights retained | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, performance, E2E |
| FWHT+MXFP4 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp4_fwht` | Normalized H32 activation transform + MXFP4 quantization; matching expert-weight basis transform/requantization | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, qualitative generation, performance, E2E; earlier 12-layer smoke |
| INT4 W4A16 accuracy reference | `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=auto` | Existing ARK WNA16 method | Full 48-layer model, quality subset |

Both expert projections, `w13` and `w2`, use the selected ARK path in prefill and
decode. Decode uses the same grouped GEMM entry points, not a separate optimized
decode kernel or a W4A16 fallback for the MXFP modes. Attention and non-MoE
linears retain their checkpoint-specific existing backends.

For the normal/FWHT ablation, both modes use the same ARK FP4 grouped GEMM.
Normal quantization uses `_quant_only=True`. FWHT transforms both expert weight
projections as `W @ H32` at loading, then requantizes them. This is a runtime
preparation step applied to the existing MXFP4 checkpoint, rather than loading
a pre-rotated checkpoint export.

### 2. Models and exact revisions

| Purpose | Model | Layers | Revision |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| MXFP8/normal MXFP4/FWHT full-model comparison | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-MXFP4-W4A4](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-MXFP4-W4A4) | 48 | `30056176cb3d122602172e39c33a0b36edda93a4` |
| Independent accuracy reference | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-INT4-W4A16](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-INT4-W4A16) | 48 | `80c3cd0bba6dbdc49d50ddeabfe232543cbd5a0a` |
| Initial loader/dispatch smoke | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-12L-MXFP4-test](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-12L-MXFP4-test) | 12 | `59a244387c2c55a085a65384280943322d36da0f` |

The MXFP4 checkpoint uses symmetric E2M1 weights, E8M0 scales, group size 32, and
`auto_round:llm_compressor` packing. The INT4 checkpoint uses symmetric integer
weights, group size 32, and `auto_round:auto_gptq` packing. **INT4 packed codes/scales
were not reinterpreted as MXFP4.** INT4 is an independent reference, not a
same-format FWHT ablation.

**The checkpoints also differ outside MoE.** A follow-up audit of both pinned
configs and tensor indexes checked all 48 layers: the INT4 checkpoint stores
all 192 attention `q/k/v/o` projections as packed INT4, while the MXFP4
checkpoint explicitly keeps those 192 projections at 16 bits. Both retain an
unquantized LM head. The INT4 accuracy reference therefore differs in attention
projection quantization as well as MoE and is not an isolated MoE-only accuracy
ablation. The MXFP8/normal/FWHT ablation retains the same non-MoE configuration.

The MXFP8 control is **MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights**, not MXFP8 weights or
a separate MXFP8 checkpoint. The `ark_mxfp8` selector changes the routed-expert
activation format to group-32 E4M3 with E8M0 scales. It retains the same original
packed MXFP4 expert weights as normal `ark_mxfp4`; neither control rotates weights.
The checkpoint name contains W4A4, but the explicit selector determines the
activation format for these routed-expert operations.

Every full-model run inspected all 48 routed MoE layers. Observed methods were
`INCARKMxfp4MoEMethod` with the requested MXFP8/normal/FWHT selector, and
`INCARKWNA16MoEMethod` for the INT4 reference.

### 3. Shared full-model settings and timing methodology

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tensor parallelism | 1 |
| Execution dtype | BF16 |
| Execution mode | Eager; graph capture disabled |
| Attention backend | `TRITON_ATTN` |
| Prefix caching | Disabled |
| Maximum model length | 2048 |
| Maximum batched tokens | 4096 |
| Maximum sequences | 8 |
| GPU memory utilization | 0.65 |
| Engine/request seed | 42 |
| Performance sampling | Greedy, fixed output length, `ignore_eos=True`, detokenization disabled |
| Warmup/timed iterations | 2 warmups + 5 timed iterations per case |

Measurements are wall-clock times for an entire offline `LLM.generate` batch,
with XPU synchronization around timed runs. They include engine scheduling,
attention, activation quantization, expert routing, and MoE GEMMs. They exclude
model loading and one-time FWHT weight preparation. Fixed synthetic input token
IDs were generated using NumPy RNG seed 42; their hashes match across the three
MXFP performance runs.
The MXFP8 control was measured in a later sequential run, not interleaved with
the original normal/FWHT runs; the runtime, GPU UUID, engine settings,
evaluation data and benchmark input hashes were checked against the originals.

These are **batch end-to-end latencies, not kernel timings, serving TTFT, or
measured TPOT**. The output-length-1 cases are prefill-heavy and output-length-64 cases are
decode-heavy, but both include all work needed for the complete request.

**Do not compare these rows as one prefill step versus one decode step.**
Generating one token normally requires one prompt forward pass; generating
64 tokens normally requires the prompt pass plus 63 sequential incremental
passes. The rows also have different input lengths (512 versus 32). A larger
total latency for the 64-output case does not by itself indicate slower
per-step decoding. Matched-input first-token and incremental-token timings
would be needed for that comparison.

### 4. Model-level performance

#### Mean batch latency

All values are seconds, reported as **mean ± sample standard deviation** over
five iterations. FWHT delta is relative to normal MXFP4; positive means slower.

| Batch | Input tokens/request | Output tokens/request | Normal MXFP4 | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | FWHT MXFP4 | FWHT latency delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 512 | 1 | 0.233271 ± 0.000345 | 0.935250 ± 0.001272 | 0.233306 ± 0.000596 | +0.015% |
| 8 | 512 | 1 | 1.049823 ± 0.017178 | 2.047423 ± 0.011420 | 1.041668 ± 0.012090 | −0.777% |
| 1 | 32 | 64 | 4.282115 ± 0.009994 | 56.819599 ± 0.021998 | 4.345646 ± 0.010423 | +1.484% |
| 8 | 32 | 64 | 6.016255 ± 0.020226 | 58.430375 ± 0.031140 | 6.214311 ± 0.012215 | +3.292% |

#### Aggregate output throughput for decode-heavy requests

Calculated as batch size × output length / mean batch latency. This includes
prefill time and is not an isolated decode-kernel rate.

| Batch | Input/output tokens per request | Normal MXFP4 (tokens/s) | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W (tokens/s) | FWHT MXFP4 (tokens/s) |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32/64 | 14.946 | 1.126 | 14.727 |
| 8 | 32/64 | 85.103 | 8.763 | 82.390 |

#### One-off engine initialization

| Configuration | Initialization including loading (s) |
| --- | ---: |
| Normal MXFP4 | 27.03 |
| MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | 30.70 |
| FWHT MXFP4 | 45.78 |

Initialization times are single observations, not repeated cold-load
benchmarks. FWHT initialization includes weight transformation/requantization.

**Interpretation:** prefill-heavy normal/FWHT results are approximately tied;
decode-heavy FWHT latency is 1.48–3.29% higher. No FWHT speedup is demonstrated.
These are preliminary measurements on one device, not a throughput
limit or a controlled measurement of FWHT arithmetic alone. Generated tokens can
change expert routing despite identical prompt IDs and sampling settings.

The MXFP8 control has **4.01× / 1.95×** normal MXFP4 latency for the batch-1 /
batch-8 prefill-heavy cases, and **13.27× / 9.71×** for the corresponding
decode-heavy cases. These are measurements of the current integration, not an
intrinsic MXFP8 hardware throughput comparison. This same-workload gap remains
even after accounting for the 64 output tokens; it is separate from the
prefill-heavy versus decode-heavy total-latency comparison.

#### Decode accounting and implementation overhead

For illustration only, divide each batch-1 32-input/64-output latency by 64:

| Configuration | Whole request (s) | E2E time divided by output tokens (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal MXFP4 | 4.282115 | 66.908 |
| MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | 56.819599 | 887.806 |
| FWHT MXFP4 | 4.345646 | 67.901 |

This normalization includes prefill and engine overhead; it is **not measured
TPOT**. For batch 8, dividing batch latency by 64 gives time per output-token
position across the batch; dividing by 512 gives aggregate time per emitted
token. Neither quantity is an isolated decode-kernel latency.

Source inspection identifies a concrete extra cost in the configured MXFP8
BDPAS path: on a staging refresh, it expands/transposes the packed E2M1 weight
payloads to FP8 staging for **all experts**, then transposes their scales.
The normal/FWHT native FP4 path reads packed weights directly and refreshes
only weight-scale staging. Workspaces are shared by shape, not resident per
layer, so switching between same-shaped layers requires staging to be refreshed
again; inference tensors without mutation counters also force refreshes.

For this 48-layer model (128 experts, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 768),
refreshing both projections in every layer entails approximately **13.5 GiB of
packed-weight reads plus 27 GiB of expanded-payload writes per forward pass**,
before scale traffic and GEMM reads. These are source-derived logical traffic
counts, not profiler measurements. Repeating this work per decode position is
a plausible major contributor to the MXFP8 gap, not an unavoidable property of
MXFP8 arithmetic. Both MXFP4 modes still use grouped prefill GEMMs for small
decode batches, and the MXFP grouped modes incur host-synchronized routing
metadata. No dedicated small-token MXFP decode implementation was validated here.

No runtime profiling breakdown was collected, so the exact contribution of
staging versus GEMM, quantization and routing remains unmeasured. The current
MXFP8 path is not a performance win in these cases.

### 5. Model accuracy and qualitative generation

The quantitative accuracy table below covers the INT4 W4A16 reference, normal
MXFP4 baseline, MXFP8-activation control and FWHT+MXFP4 configuration, using the
same evaluation subsets and settings. Generation examples remain qualitative
smoke checks, not evidence of accuracy equivalence.

#### Evaluation methodology

- **WikiText-2 subset:** first 8192 token IDs of the test split, split into
  sixteen non-overlapping 512-token chunks. The first token in each chunk is
  unscored, giving **8176 scored tokens**. PPL is computed from actual prompt-token
  log probabilities. This is not a full WikiText-2 benchmark or sliding-window PPL.
- **GSM8K subset:** first 32 test questions, zero-shot chat, thinking disabled,
  greedy decoding, seed 42, maximum 256 generated tokens per question. Numerical
  answer extraction reuses the existing vLLM evaluation helper, which extracts
  the last number; therefore truncation can materially affect the score.
- **Qualitative generation:** six prompts covering English QA, multiplication,
  English-to-Chinese translation, Chinese explanation, Python generation, and
  simple word arithmetic. Thinking disabled, greedy, maximum 128 output tokens.

| Metric | INT4 W4A16 reference | Normal MXFP4 | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | FWHT+MXFP4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| WikiText-2 subset PPL ↓ | 13.337441 | 15.067995 | 13.680705 | 15.901194 |
| Mean negative log-likelihood per scored token ↓ | 2.590575 | 2.712573 | 2.615986 | 2.766394 |
| Scored PPL tokens | 8176 | 8176 | 8176 | 8176 |
| GSM8K correct / total | 23 / 32 | 23 / 32 | 24 / 32 | 23 / 32 |
| GSM8K subset accuracy | 71.875% | 71.875% | 75.000% | 71.875% |
| GSM8K outputs hitting the 256-token limit | 12 | 11 | 12 | 9 |

MXFP8 activation PPL is 9.21% lower than normal MXFP4 on this fixed subset.
Its GSM8K result differs by one answer (+3.125 percentage points); this small,
generation-limited sample does not establish a general accuracy improvement.

FWHT+MXFP4 PPL is 5.53% higher than normal MXFP4 on this subset. Both score
23/32 on GSM8K, but their extracted final answers agree on 25/32 questions;
equal aggregate scores do not establish accuracy equivalence.

The GSM8K sample is small, not random, and includes truncated answers. These
are preliminary subset results, not full benchmark scores. No BF16 accuracy
reference or full benchmark was run.

All four full-model configurations completed six qualitative prompts with
finite generated-token log probabilities.

All four full-model configurations produced these shared responses:

| Prompt/task | Observed response |
| --- | --- |
| Capital of France | The capital of France is Paris. |
| 17 × 23 | 17 * 23 = 391 |
| Translate “Machine learning helps computers learn from data.” into Chinese | 机器学习帮助计算机从数据中学习。 |

The FWHT response to the Chinese sky-color question was:

> 白天的天空呈现蓝色是因为阳光中的短波长蓝光在大气中被散射得更多。这种散射现象被称为瑞利散射，使得蓝色光线从各个方向传播到我们的眼睛。

The previous 12-layer checkpoint produced incoherent text. It is a truncated
loader/kernel smoke model, **not an accuracy reference**. Finite logprobs and
successful execution of that checkpoint were never sufficient for accuracy
acceptance. Complete-model generation now produces coherent output, but this
does not isolate every cause of the earlier behavior or prove a terminal
encoding issue.

#### Dataset provenance

| Dataset | Pinned revision | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1 | `b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3` | Test split, first 8192 token IDs |
| openai/gsm8k, main | `740312add88f781978c0658806c59bc2815b9866` | Test split, first 32 rows |

The INT4 and MXFP4 tokenizer files differ, but the 8192 PPL input IDs were
verified identical. PPL input-ID SHA256:
`62fac9978188405c124bad80d0c36b988c66c164b20b65e668f8bc1bd4859c75`.
Combined cached evaluation-data SHA256:
`ce71d3bad4a5ffa9d8c821034a67b61b858070a2ef40d1997513ad81eeb609b6`.

### 6. Test results

Results below describe separate suites/runs, not an additive count of unique tests.

| Validation | Device / scope | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused ARK MXFP4 adapter unit tests, including the normal quant-only path | CPU | 23 passed |
| Expanded CPU-visible vLLM AutoRound regression suite | CPU | 131 passed, 14 skipped, 9 deselected |
| CPU-visible ARK MoE suite, earlier run | CPU | 9 passed, 138 skipped; skips are not device validation |
| Native ARK MXFP MoE tests | GPU 7 | 21 passed, 126 deselected |
| Complete FWHT/MXFP4 quantizer numerical suite | GPU 7 | 168 passed |
| MXFP8/FWHT 12-layer model integration smoke | GPU 7 | 2 passed, 146 deselected |
| Normal/FWHT full 48-layer model E2Es | GPU 6 | 2 passed, 152 deselected |
| MXFP8 × MXFP4 full 48-layer model E2E, separate run | GPU 6 | 1 passed, 153 deselected |

The model E2Es check every routed MoE layer and packed layout, mixed-length
prefill, eight forced decode tokens, repeated requests with a different batch
shape, and finite sampled-token logprobs. The earlier 12-layer tests inspected
all 12 MoE layers/24 expert projection tensors; the complete-model tests
inspected all 48 routed MoE layers.

Relevant Ruff, formatting, Markdown and whitespace checks passed. Other
integration checks run earlier included mypy, typos, SPDX and test tethering;
the focused AutoRound pre-commit checks passed. The full vLLM all-hooks bootstrap
did not complete because an unrelated actionlint installation stalled; this
report does not claim that every repository hook passed.

### 7. Known limitations and unsupported configurations

- The native XPU W4A16 reference attempt was rejected by the installed
  `XPUExperts` implementation because it supports Xe2/Xe3, not CRI. Architecture
  checks were not bypassed. The successful INT4 run uses ARK WNA16.
- The default native INC MXFP4 `auto` backend was not benchmarked. The normal
  baseline in these tables is explicitly **ARK `ark_mxfp4`**, not `auto`.
- Triton attention was selected because the installed XPU FlashAttention wheel
  rejects CRI. The MoE GEMMs still use ARK CRI BDPAS.
- ARK grouped routing metadata requires host synchronization: eager execution
  is required and graph capture is unsupported.
- Optional static routing caches were disabled because native device writes do
  not increment the mutation counter those caches use.
- TP=1 only was validated. TP>1, expert parallelism, production serving load,
  long-context behavior, and full benchmark accuracy were not validated.
- INT4 is an independent accuracy reference, not a MoE-only accuracy ablation:
  its attention projections are also INT4, unlike those in the MXFP4 model.
- The FWHT path does not accept a pre-rotated checkpoint format; it transforms
  and requantizes expert weights at loading.
- No kernel-only performance comparison, matched-input TTFT/TPOT measurement,
  or runtime profiling breakdown of the MXFP8 latency gap is included. The
  staging discussion above is source analysis, not a measured attribution.

### Conclusion

The integration is exercised on real CRI hardware, including successful native
kernel tests and complete-model MXFP8/normal/FWHT runs. It establishes a working
end-to-end calling path. The current model-level measurements show near-tied
prefill-heavy batch latency and modestly slower FWHT decode-heavy latency; a performance
win is not demonstrated in these cases. The MXFP8-activation control has lower
subset PPL than normal MXFP4 but substantially higher latency in the current
implementation. Quantitative accuracy figures reported here cover INT4 W4A16,
normal MXFP4, MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights and FWHT+MXFP4; they are not full
benchmarks.

AI assistance disclosure: implementation, test execution, and report preparation
were assisted by GitHub Copilot; human review is required before submission.

@@ -29,6 +29,43 @@ On Intel platforms, AutoRound recipes are being enabled progressively by format
 
 Additional recipes and formats will be supported in future releases.
 
+### Experimental CRI MXFP4 routed experts
+
+For symmetric group-32 E2M1/E8M0 MoE checkpoints with
+`auto_round:llm_compressor` packing, an installed CRI ARK build can be selected
+explicitly with `VLLM_XPU_INC_MXFP4_BACKEND`:
+
+- `auto`: retain the existing vLLM backend selection.
+- `ark_mxfp4`: raw activation MXFP4 quantization and native FP4 grouped GEMM.
+- `ark_mxfp8`: dynamic E4M3/E8M0 activations with the original MXFP4 weights.
+- `ark_mxfp4_fwht`: normalized H32 activation transform and MXFP4 quantization;
+  both expert weight projections are transformed and requantized at loading.
+
+These opt-in paths require eager execution, TP/EP/DP/SP=1, and unshared,

+no optimized small-token decode implementation or performance gain is implied.

+"""Explicit CRI MXFP activation controls for packed MXFP4 checkpoints."""
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import envs
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import (
+    ApplyMoEActivationConfig,
+    MoEActivation,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
+    FusedMoEConfig,
+    FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe_method_base import (
+    FusedMoEMethodBase,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import (
+    move_parameter,
+    replace_parameter,
+    set_weight_attrs,
+)
+
+from .inc_wna16_moe import INCARKWNA16MoEMethod
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def dequantize_mxfp4(codes: torch.Tensor, scales: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Decode checkpoint low-nibble-first E2M1 and E8M0 independently."""
+    levels = torch.tensor(
+        [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0],
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device=codes.device,
+    )
+    raw = codes.to(torch.int32)
+    raw = torch.stack((raw & 15, raw >> 4), dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+    values = levels[raw & 7] * torch.where((raw & 8) != 0, -1.0, 1.0)
+    exponents = (scales.to(torch.int32) - 127).repeat_interleave(32, dim=-1)
+    return torch.ldexp(values, exponents)
+
+
+class INCARKMxfp4MoEMethod(INCARKWNA16MoEMethod):
+    """Reuse ARK's XPU routing/activation/gather with native MXFP GEMMs.
+
+    Only eager TP=1, EP=1, unshared SiLU experts are supported. Both expert
+    projections use the same selected activation format in prefill and decode.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, moe: FusedMoEConfig, backend: str) -> None:
+        FusedMoEMethodBase.__init__(self, moe)
+        if backend not in ("ark_mxfp8", "ark_mxfp4", "ark_mxfp4_fwht"):
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ARK MXFP4 backend: {backend}")
+        if (
+            moe.tp_size != 1
+            or moe.ep_size != 1
+            or moe.dp_size != 1
+            or moe.sp_size != 1
+            or moe.shared_expert_prefix is not None
+            or moe.activation != MoEActivation.SILU
+            or moe.has_bias
+        ):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ARK MXFP4 MoE supports unshared, bias-free SiLU, TP/EP/DP/SP=1"
+            )
+        import auto_round_kernel as ark
+
+        lib = getattr(ark, "xpu_lib", None)
+        if getattr(lib, "sycl_target", None) not in ("cri", "intel_gpu_cri"):
+            raise NotImplementedError("ARK MXFP4 MoE requires a CRI ARK build")
+        required = (
+            "moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp4_mxfp4",
+            "moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp8_mxfp4",
+            "moe_gemm_prefill_hmt_mxfp4_mxfp4",
+            "mxfp8_quant",
+        )
+        if not all(hasattr(ark, name) for name in required):
+            raise ImportError("ARK native MXFP quantization/GEMM APIs are missing")
+        self.use_prepacked_weights = (
+            envs.VLLM_XPU_INC_MXFP8_PREPACK
+            if backend == "ark_mxfp8"
+            else envs.VLLM_XPU_INC_MXFP4_PREPACK
+        )
+        prepared_prefix = "mxfp8_mxfp4" if backend == "ark_mxfp8" else "mxfp4_mxfp4"
+        if self.use_prepacked_weights and not all(
+            hasattr(ark, name)
+            for name in (
+                f"moe_{prepared_prefix}_prepack",
+                f"moe_gemm_prefill_{prepared_prefix}_prepacked",
+            )
+        ):
+            raise ImportError("ARK prepared MXFP weight APIs are missing")
+        self.ark = ark
+        self.backend = backend
+        self.prepared_weights: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        self.group_size = 32
+        self.local_num_experts = None
+        self.global_num_experts = None
+        self.expert_map = None
+        self.rows_per_expert = None
+        self.unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row = None
+        self.router_weight_ones = None
+        self.router_weights_fn = self._keep_router_weights
+        self.activation = moe.activation
+        self.activation_config = ApplyMoEActivationConfig.from_configs(
+            moe, FusedMoEQuantConfig.make()
+        )
+        self.inter_size = moe.intermediate_size_per_partition
+        self.inter_size_scale = 1
+        self.remap_hidden_states_op = torch.ops._moe_C.remap_hidden_states
+        self.moe_gather_op = torch.ops._moe_C.moe_gather
+        self.w13_codes = None
+        self.w13_scales = None
+        self.w2_codes = None
+        self.w2_scales = None
+        logger.info_once("Using native CRI ARK MoE activation control: %s", backend)
+
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        num_experts: int,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        intermediate_size_per_partition: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs,
+    ) -> None:
+        layer.num_experts = num_experts
+        layer.params_dtype = params_dtype
+        projections = (
+            (
+                "w13",
+                self.moe.w13_num_shards * intermediate_size_per_partition,
+                hidden_size,
+            ),
+            ("w2", hidden_size, intermediate_size_per_partition),
+        )
+        for projection, n, k in projections:
+            for suffix, width in (("packed", k // 2), ("scale", k // 32)):
+                parameter = torch.nn.Parameter(
+                    torch.empty(num_experts, n, width, dtype=torch.uint8),
+                    requires_grad=False,
+                )
+                layer.register_parameter(f"{projection}_weight_{suffix}", parameter)
+                attrs = dict(extra_weight_attrs)
+                if suffix == "scale":
+                    attrs["quant_method"] = FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.GROUP.value
+                set_weight_attrs(parameter, attrs)
+
+    def get_fused_moe_quant_config(self, layer) -> None:
+        # Quantization is performed inside the ARK calls, not the modular kernel.
+        return None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer) -> None:
+        for projection in ("w13", "w2"):
+            move_parameter(layer, f"{projection}_weight_packed", f"{projection}_weight")
+            weight = getattr(layer, f"{projection}_weight").detach().contiguous()
+            scales = getattr(layer, f"{projection}_weight_scale").detach().contiguous()
+            if weight.dtype != torch.uint8 or scales.dtype != torch.uint8:
+                raise ValueError("ARK MXFP4 requires uint8 E2M1/E8M0 weights")
+            if weight.shape[-1] * 2 % 64 or scales.shape[-1] * 16 != weight.shape[-1]:
+                raise ValueError("ARK MXFP4 requires K divisible by 64 and group32")
+            if self.backend == "ark_mxfp4_fwht":
+                from auto_round_kernel.mxfp4_hadamard import mxfp4_hadamard_quant
+
+                # Bound temporary storage: W@H32 followed by group32 requantization.
+                for expert in range(weight.shape[0]):
+                    source = dequantize_mxfp4(weight[expert], scales[expert])
+                    rotated, new_scales = mxfp4_hadamard_quant(
+                        source.to(torch.bfloat16)
+                    )
+                    weight[expert].copy_(rotated)
+                    scales[expert].copy_(new_scales)
+            replace_parameter(layer, f"{projection}_weight", weight)
+            replace_parameter(layer, f"{projection}_weight_scale", scales)
+            setattr(self, f"{projection}_codes", weight)
+            setattr(self, f"{projection}_scales", scales)
+            if self.use_prepacked_weights:
+                prepare = (
+                    self.ark.moe_mxfp8_mxfp4_prepack
+                    if self.backend == "ark_mxfp8"
+                    else self.ark.moe_mxfp4_mxfp4_prepack
+                )
+                self.prepared_weights[projection] = prepare(
+                    weight, scales, group_size=32
+                )
+
+        if layer.expert_map is not None or layer.apply_router_weight_on_input:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ARK MXFP4 requires local output-weighted routing"
+            )
+        assert self.w13_codes is not None
+        self.local_num_experts = self.w13_codes.shape[0]
+        self.global_num_experts = layer.global_num_experts
+        self.expert_map = layer.expert_map
+        self.rows_per_expert = torch.empty(
+            self.local_num_experts, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.w13_codes.device
+        )
+
+    def _check_moe_weights_loaded(self) -> None:
+        assert self.w13_codes is not None and self.w2_codes is not None
+        assert self.w13_scales is not None and self.w2_scales is not None
+
+    def _project(self, x, codes, scales, routing):
+        kwargs = {"output_dtype": x.dtype, "group_size": 32}
+        if self.backend == "ark_mxfp4_fwht":
+            return self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_hmt_mxfp4_mxfp4(
+                x, codes, scales, routing, **kwargs
+            )
+        if self.backend == "ark_mxfp8":
+            quantized, act_scales = self.ark.mxfp8_quant(x)
+            gemm = self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp8_mxfp4
+        else:
+            from auto_round_kernel.mxfp4_hadamard import mxfp4_hadamard_quant
+
+            quantized, act_scales = mxfp4_hadamard_quant(x, _quant_only=True)
+            gemm = self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp4_mxfp4
+        return gemm(quantized, act_scales, codes, scales, routing, **kwargs)
+
+    def _apply_w13_moe(self, x, rows_per_expert):
+        if self.use_prepacked_weights:
+            return self._apply_prepared_projection(x, "w13", rows_per_expert)
+        return self._project(x, self.w13_codes, self.w13_scales, rows_per_expert)
+
+    def _apply_w2_moe(self, x, rows_per_expert):
+        if self.use_prepacked_weights:
+            return self._apply_prepared_projection(x, "w2", rows_per_expert)
+        return self._project(x, self.w2_codes, self.w2_scales, rows_per_expert)
+
+    def _apply_prepared_projection(self, x, projection, routing):
+        prepared = self.prepared_weights[projection]
+        if self.backend == "ark_mxfp8":
+            return self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp8_mxfp4_prepacked(
+                *self.ark.mxfp8_quant(x), prepared, routing
+            )
+        if self.backend == "ark_mxfp4_fwht":
+            return self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_hmt_mxfp4_mxfp4_prepacked(
+                x, prepared, routing
+            )
+        from auto_round_kernel.mxfp4_hadamard import mxfp4_hadamard_quant
+
+        return self.ark.moe_gemm_prefill_mxfp4_mxfp4_prepacked(
+            *mxfp4_hadamard_quant(x, _quant_only=True), prepared, routing
+        )

+import os
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context, is_forward_context_available
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import FusedMoEConfig

+

+
+W4A8_MOE_SYMBOLS = ("moe_w4a8_prepack", "moe_gemm_w4a8")
+W4A16_DECODE_SYMBOLS = ("moe_gemm_decode",)
+_MOE_AUTO_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS = 128
+_EAGER_PREPACK_VALUES = {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}
+_EAGER_PREPACK_FORCE_VALUES = {"force", "always"}
+
+
+def _has_ark_symbols(is_ark_available: bool, ark, symbols: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
+    xpu_lib = getattr(ark, "xpu_lib", None) if ark is not None else None
+    return (
+        is_ark_available
+        and ark is not None
+        and xpu_lib is not None
+        and all(hasattr(ark, symbol) and hasattr(xpu_lib, symbol) for symbol in symbols)
+    )
+
+
+def has_ark_w4a8_moe_kernel(is_ark_available: bool, ark) -> bool:
+    return _has_ark_symbols(
+        is_ark_available,
+        ark,
+        W4A8_MOE_SYMBOLS + W4A16_DECODE_SYMBOLS,
+    )
+
+
+def _tensor_parallel_world_size() -> int:
+    try:
+        from vllm.distributed import get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size
+
+        return get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    except (AssertionError, RuntimeError, ValueError):
+        return 1
+
+
+def _w4a8_eager_prepack_enabled() -> bool:
+    value = os.environ.get("ARK_MOE_W4A8_EAGER_PREPACK", "")
+    normalized = value.strip().lower()
+    if normalized in _EAGER_PREPACK_FORCE_VALUES:
+        return True
+    if normalized not in _EAGER_PREPACK_VALUES:
+        return False
+
+    if _tensor_parallel_world_size() > 1:
+        return True
+
+    logger.info_once(
+        "ARK W4A8 MoE eager prepack is disabled for "
+        "tensor_parallel_size=1; use "
+        "ARK_MOE_W4A8_EAGER_PREPACK=force to override."
+    )
+    return False
+
+
+def _moe_auto_decode_max_total_tokens() -> int:
+    value = os.environ.get("ARK_MOE_AUTO_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS")
+    if value is None:
+        return _MOE_AUTO_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS
+    try:
+        threshold = int(value.strip())
+    except ValueError:
+        return _MOE_AUTO_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS
+    if threshold <= 0:
+        return _MOE_AUTO_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS
+    return threshold
+
+
+def _first_attention_metadata():
+    if not is_forward_context_available():
+        return None
+
+    attn_metadata = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
+    if isinstance(attn_metadata, list):
+        entries = attn_metadata
+    else:
+        entries = [attn_metadata]
+
+    for entry in entries:
+        if isinstance(entry, dict):
+            for metadata in entry.values():
+                if metadata is not None:
+                    return metadata
+        elif entry is not None:
+            return entry
+    return None
+
+
+def _prefill_decode_split(num_rows: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    metadata = _first_attention_metadata()
+    if metadata is None:
+        return None
+
+    num_decode_tokens = getattr(metadata, "num_decode_tokens", None)
+    num_prefill_tokens = getattr(metadata, "num_prefill_tokens", None)
+    if num_decode_tokens is None or num_prefill_tokens is None:
+        return None
+
+    num_decode_tokens = int(num_decode_tokens)
+    num_prefill_tokens = int(num_prefill_tokens)
+    if num_decode_tokens < 0 or num_prefill_tokens < 0:
+        return None
+    if num_decode_tokens + num_prefill_tokens != num_rows:
+        return None
+    return num_decode_tokens, num_prefill_tokens
+
+
+def _effective_moe_group_size(
+    layer_config: "INCLayerConfig",
+    hidden_size: int,
+    intermediate_size: int,
+    prefix: str,
+) -> int:
+    group_size = layer_config.group_size
+    while intermediate_size % group_size or hidden_size % group_size:
+        group_size //= 2
+        if group_size < 32:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=w4a8 requires hidden and "
+                "intermediate sizes divisible by a derived group size of at "
+                f"least 32. Layer: {prefix}."
+            )
+    return group_size
+
+
+def check_xpu_moe_w4a8_supported(
+    layer: "torch.nn.Module",
+    layer_config: "INCLayerConfig",
+    prefix: str,
+) -> int:
+    moe_config = layer.moe_config
+    hidden_size = moe_config.hidden_dim
+    intermediate_size = moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition
+    group_size = _effective_moe_group_size(
+        layer_config,
+        hidden_size,
+        intermediate_size,
+        prefix,
+    )
+
+    if group_size <= 0 or group_size % 8 != 0:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            "VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=w4a8 requires a MoE group size that "
+            f"is a positive multiple of 8, got {group_size}. Layer: {prefix}."
+        )
+
+    gemm_shapes = (
+        (
+            "w13",
+            moe_config.w13_num_shards * intermediate_size,
+            hidden_size,
+        ),
+        ("w2", hidden_size, intermediate_size),
+    )
+    for name, out_features, in_features in gemm_shapes:
+        if out_features % 16 != 0 or in_features % 64 != 0:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=w4a8 requires MoE GEMM shapes "
+                "with N multiple of 16 and K multiple of 64, got "
+                f"{name}: N={out_features}, K={in_features}. Layer: {prefix}."
+            )
+        if in_features % group_size != 0:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=w4a8 requires K to be divisible "
+                f"by group_size, got {name}: K={in_features}, "
+                f"group_size={group_size}. Layer: {prefix}."
+            )
+    return group_size
+
+
+class INCARKW4A8MoEMethod(INCARKWNA16MoEMethod):
+    kernel_name = "W4A8"
+    log_message = "Selected ARK XPU W4A8 prefill/W4A16 decode MoE method."
+    prefill_kernel_log_message = "Using ARK XPU W4A8 MoE kernel for prefill."
+    decode_kernel_log_message = "Using ARK XPU W4A16 MoE kernel for decode."
+    _eager_prepack_layer_count = 0
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        quant_config: MoeWNA16Config,
+        moe: FusedMoEConfig,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(quant_config, moe)
+        self.w13_moe_w4a8: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int] | None = None
+        self.w2_moe_w4a8: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int] | None = None
+        self.w13_moe_w4a16: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int] | None = None
+        self.w2_moe_w4a16: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int] | None = None
+        self.w13_moe_w4a8_prepacked: tuple[
+            torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int
+        ] | None = None

+                True,
+                layer,
+                x,

+                topk_ids,

+        if num_prefill_tokens == 0:

+                False,
+                layer,
+                x,
+                topk_weights,
+                topk_ids,
+                shared_experts,

+        )
+        output[:num_decode_tokens].copy_(decode_output)
+        del decode_output
+
+        prefill_output = self._apply_with_prefill_kernel(
+            True,
+            layer,
+            x[num_decode_tokens:],
+            topk_weights[num_decode_tokens:],
+            topk_ids[num_decode_tokens:],
+            shared_experts,
+            shared_experts_input,
+        )
+        output[num_decode_tokens:].copy_(prefill_output)
+        del prefill_output
+        return output

## CRI MXFP MoE integration: hardware validation, model performance and accuracy controls

### Summary

- Native ARK CRI kernels were built successfully and exercised through vLLM.
- MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights passed real-device kernel/model smoke tests
  and now also have a complete 48-layer model evaluation.
- MXFP8, normal MXFP4 and FWHT+MXFP4 use the same complete 48-layer
  Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP4 checkpoint, with an independent INT4 W4A16 accuracy reference.
- All four complete-model configurations produced coherent English/Chinese responses.
- The MXFP8-activation control measured PPL **13.680705** and GSM8K **24/32
  (75.000%)** on the fixed subsets. It was slower than normal MXFP4 in every
  timed case; decode-heavy batch latency was **9.71–13.27×** normal MXFP4.
- **No model-level FWHT speedup was demonstrated:** prefill-heavy cases were
  approximately tied; decode-heavy cases had 1.48–3.29% higher latency.
- Quantitative accuracy results in this comment cover the INT4 W4A16 reference,
  normal MXFP4 baseline, MXFP8-activation control and FWHT+MXFP4 configuration.
  These are preliminary subset results; no accuracy-equivalence claim is made.
- Performance results shown here cover only MXFP8, normal MXFP4 and FWHT+MXFP4;
  INT4 W4A16 is retained only as an accuracy reference.

### 1. Environment and implementation

| Item | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Linux, Docker container `moe` |
| Device | Intel CRI, reported as Intel Graphics `0x674F`, 121.59 GiB |
| Full-model comparison | Physical GPU 6 only, exposed as logical device 0 |
| Earlier native-kernel/smoke tests | Physical GPU 7 only, separate from GPU 6 comparisons |
| Device isolation | `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6`, `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu` for the comparison |
| PyTorch | Custom CRI `2.14.0a0+gitd35bb04` |
| Triton | `3.8.0+git2f96b0eb` |
| DPC++ | 2026.2.0 |
| vLLM XPU kernels | `0.1.15.4` |
| vLLM integration branch | `feat/cri-mxfp4-moe`, based on `zhenzhong/w4a8_moe` |
| AutoRound integration branch | `feat/cri-mxfp4-moe-integration`, based on `feat/mxfp8-mxfp4-moe-bdpas` |

The tested source snapshots include uncommitted integration changes; the base
branch HEADs are not immutable identifiers for the complete tested patch.
The existing custom CRI PyTorch/Triton wheels were preserved.

The full ARK XPU extension compiled and linked successfully (289 build steps).
Runtime capability checks confirmed `sycl_target=cri` and `has_mxfp_bdpas=True`.
Compatible external CRI block-scaled headers were used only for the BDPAS
translation unit; the pinned SYCL-TLA headers were retained for ordinary kernels.

| Mode | Selector | Routed-expert computation | Coverage reported here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MXFP8 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp8` | Dynamic group-32 E4M3 activations × E2M1 weights | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, performance, E2E; native tests and earlier 12-layer smoke |
| Normal MXFP4 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp4` | Raw activations quantized to MXFP4, without FWHT; original packed weights retained | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, performance, E2E |
| FWHT+MXFP4 × MXFP4 | `ark_mxfp4_fwht` | Normalized H32 activation transform + MXFP4 quantization; matching expert-weight basis transform/requantization | Full 48-layer model, quality subset, qualitative generation, performance, E2E; earlier 12-layer smoke |
| INT4 W4A16 accuracy reference | `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND=auto` | Existing ARK WNA16 method | Full 48-layer model, quality subset |

Both expert projections, `w13` and `w2`, use the selected ARK path in prefill and
decode. Decode uses the same grouped GEMM entry points, not a separate optimized
decode kernel or a W4A16 fallback for the MXFP modes. Attention and non-MoE
linears retain their checkpoint-specific existing backends.

For the normal/FWHT ablation, both modes use the same ARK FP4 grouped GEMM.
Normal quantization uses `_quant_only=True`. FWHT transforms both expert weight
projections as `W @ H32` at loading, then requantizes them. This is a runtime
preparation step applied to the existing MXFP4 checkpoint, rather than loading
a pre-rotated checkpoint export.

### 2. Models and exact revisions

| Purpose | Model | Layers | Revision |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| MXFP8/normal MXFP4/FWHT full-model comparison | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-MXFP4-W4A4](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-MXFP4-W4A4) | 48 | `30056176cb3d122602172e39c33a0b36edda93a4` |
| Independent accuracy reference | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-INT4-W4A16](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-AutoRound-INT4-W4A16) | 48 | `80c3cd0bba6dbdc49d50ddeabfe232543cbd5a0a` |
| Initial loader/dispatch smoke | [INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-12L-MXFP4-test](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-30B-A3B-12L-MXFP4-test) | 12 | `59a244387c2c55a085a65384280943322d36da0f` |

The MXFP4 checkpoint uses symmetric E2M1 weights, E8M0 scales, group size 32, and
`auto_round:llm_compressor` packing. The INT4 checkpoint uses symmetric integer
weights, group size 32, and `auto_round:auto_gptq` packing. **INT4 packed codes/scales
were not reinterpreted as MXFP4.** INT4 is an independent reference, not a
same-format FWHT ablation.

**The checkpoints also differ outside MoE.** A follow-up audit of both pinned
configs and tensor indexes checked all 48 layers: the INT4 checkpoint stores
all 192 attention `q/k/v/o` projections as packed INT4, while the MXFP4
checkpoint explicitly keeps those 192 projections at 16 bits. Both retain an
unquantized LM head. The INT4 accuracy reference therefore differs in attention
projection quantization as well as MoE and is not an isolated MoE-only accuracy
ablation. The MXFP8/normal/FWHT ablation retains the same non-MoE configuration.

The MXFP8 control is **MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights**, not MXFP8 weights or
a separate MXFP8 checkpoint. The `ark_mxfp8` selector changes the routed-expert
activation format to group-32 E4M3 with E8M0 scales. It retains the same original
packed MXFP4 expert weights as normal `ark_mxfp4`; neither control rotates weights.
The checkpoint name contains W4A4, but the explicit selector determines the
activation format for these routed-expert operations.

Every full-model run inspected all 48 routed MoE layers. Observed methods were
`INCARKMxfp4MoEMethod` with the requested MXFP8/normal/FWHT selector, and
`INCARKWNA16MoEMethod` for the INT4 reference.

### 3. Shared full-model settings and timing methodology

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tensor parallelism | 1 |
| Execution dtype | BF16 |
| Execution mode | Eager; graph capture disabled |
| Attention backend | `TRITON_ATTN` |
| Prefix caching | Disabled |
| Maximum model length | 2048 |
| Maximum batched tokens | 4096 |
| Maximum sequences | 8 |
| GPU memory utilization | 0.65 |
| Engine/request seed | 42 |
| Performance sampling | Greedy, fixed output length, `ignore_eos=True`, detokenization disabled |
| Warmup/timed iterations | 2 warmups + 5 timed iterations per case |

Measurements are wall-clock times for an entire offline `LLM.generate` batch,
with XPU synchronization around timed runs. They include engine scheduling,
attention, activation quantization, expert routing, and MoE GEMMs. They exclude
model loading and one-time FWHT weight preparation. Fixed synthetic input token
IDs were generated using NumPy RNG seed 42; their hashes match across the three
MXFP performance runs.
The MXFP8 control was measured in a later sequential run, not interleaved with
the original normal/FWHT runs; the runtime, GPU UUID, engine settings,
evaluation data and benchmark input hashes were checked against the originals.

These are **batch end-to-end latencies, not kernel timings, serving TTFT, or
measured TPOT**. The output-length-1 cases are prefill-heavy and output-length-64 cases are
decode-heavy, but both include all work needed for the complete request.

**Do not compare these rows as one prefill step versus one decode step.**
Generating one token normally requires one prompt forward pass; generating
64 tokens normally requires the prompt pass plus 63 sequential incremental
passes. The rows also have different input lengths (512 versus 32). A larger
total latency for the 64-output case does not by itself indicate slower
per-step decoding. Matched-input first-token and incremental-token timings
would be needed for that comparison.

### 4. Model-level performance

#### Mean batch latency

All values are seconds, reported as **mean ± sample standard deviation** over
five iterations. FWHT delta is relative to normal MXFP4; positive means slower.

| Batch | Input tokens/request | Output tokens/request | Normal MXFP4 | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | FWHT MXFP4 | FWHT latency delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 512 | 1 | 0.233271 ± 0.000345 | 0.935250 ± 0.001272 | 0.233306 ± 0.000596 | +0.015% |
| 8 | 512 | 1 | 1.049823 ± 0.017178 | 2.047423 ± 0.011420 | 1.041668 ± 0.012090 | −0.777% |
| 1 | 32 | 64 | 4.282115 ± 0.009994 | 56.819599 ± 0.021998 | 4.345646 ± 0.010423 | +1.484% |
| 8 | 32 | 64 | 6.016255 ± 0.020226 | 58.430375 ± 0.031140 | 6.214311 ± 0.012215 | +3.292% |

#### Aggregate output throughput for decode-heavy requests

Calculated as batch size × output length / mean batch latency. This includes
prefill time and is not an isolated decode-kernel rate.

| Batch | Input/output tokens per request | Normal MXFP4 (tokens/s) | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W (tokens/s) | FWHT MXFP4 (tokens/s) |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32/64 | 14.946 | 1.126 | 14.727 |
| 8 | 32/64 | 85.103 | 8.763 | 82.390 |

#### One-off engine initialization

| Configuration | Initialization including loading (s) |
| --- | ---: |
| Normal MXFP4 | 27.03 |
| MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | 30.70 |
| FWHT MXFP4 | 45.78 |

Initialization times are single observations, not repeated cold-load
benchmarks. FWHT initialization includes weight transformation/requantization.

**Interpretation:** prefill-heavy normal/FWHT results are approximately tied;
decode-heavy FWHT latency is 1.48–3.29% higher. No FWHT speedup is demonstrated.
These are preliminary measurements on one device, not a throughput
limit or a controlled measurement of FWHT arithmetic alone. Generated tokens can
change expert routing despite identical prompt IDs and sampling settings.

The MXFP8 control has **4.01× / 1.95×** normal MXFP4 latency for the batch-1 /
batch-8 prefill-heavy cases, and **13.27× / 9.71×** for the corresponding
decode-heavy cases. These are measurements of the current integration, not an
intrinsic MXFP8 hardware throughput comparison. This same-workload gap remains
even after accounting for the 64 output tokens; it is separate from the
prefill-heavy versus decode-heavy total-latency comparison.

#### Decode accounting and implementation overhead

For illustration only, divide each batch-1 32-input/64-output latency by 64:

| Configuration | Whole request (s) | E2E time divided by output tokens (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal MXFP4 | 4.282115 | 66.908 |
| MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | 56.819599 | 887.806 |
| FWHT MXFP4 | 4.345646 | 67.901 |

This normalization includes prefill and engine overhead; it is **not measured
TPOT**. For batch 8, dividing batch latency by 64 gives time per output-token
position across the batch; dividing by 512 gives aggregate time per emitted
token. Neither quantity is an isolated decode-kernel latency.

Source inspection identifies a concrete extra cost in the configured MXFP8
BDPAS path: on a staging refresh, it expands/transposes the packed E2M1 weight
payloads to FP8 staging for **all experts**, then transposes their scales.
The normal/FWHT native FP4 path reads packed weights directly and refreshes
only weight-scale staging. Workspaces are shared by shape, not resident per
layer, so switching between same-shaped layers requires staging to be refreshed
again; inference tensors without mutation counters also force refreshes.

For this 48-layer model (128 experts, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 768),
refreshing both projections in every layer entails approximately **13.5 GiB of
packed-weight reads plus 27 GiB of expanded-payload writes per forward pass**,
before scale traffic and GEMM reads. These are source-derived logical traffic
counts, not profiler measurements. Repeating this work per decode position is
a plausible major contributor to the MXFP8 gap, not an unavoidable property of
MXFP8 arithmetic. Both MXFP4 modes still use grouped prefill GEMMs for small
decode batches, and the MXFP grouped modes incur host-synchronized routing
metadata. No dedicated small-token MXFP decode implementation was validated here.

No runtime profiling breakdown was collected, so the exact contribution of
staging versus GEMM, quantization and routing remains unmeasured. The current
MXFP8 path is not a performance win in these cases.

### 5. Model accuracy and qualitative generation

The quantitative accuracy table below covers the INT4 W4A16 reference, normal
MXFP4 baseline, MXFP8-activation control and FWHT+MXFP4 configuration, using the
same evaluation subsets and settings. Generation examples remain qualitative
smoke checks, not evidence of accuracy equivalence.

#### Evaluation methodology

- **WikiText-2 subset:** first 8192 token IDs of the test split, split into
  sixteen non-overlapping 512-token chunks. The first token in each chunk is
  unscored, giving **8176 scored tokens**. PPL is computed from actual prompt-token
  log probabilities. This is not a full WikiText-2 benchmark or sliding-window PPL.
- **GSM8K subset:** first 32 test questions, zero-shot chat, thinking disabled,
  greedy decoding, seed 42, maximum 256 generated tokens per question. Numerical
  answer extraction reuses the existing vLLM evaluation helper, which extracts
  the last number; therefore truncation can materially affect the score.
- **Qualitative generation:** six prompts covering English QA, multiplication,
  English-to-Chinese translation, Chinese explanation, Python generation, and
  simple word arithmetic. Thinking disabled, greedy, maximum 128 output tokens.

| Metric | INT4 W4A16 reference | Normal MXFP4 | MXFP8 A × MXFP4 W | FWHT+MXFP4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| WikiText-2 subset PPL ↓ | 13.337441 | 15.067995 | 13.680705 | 15.901194 |
| Mean negative log-likelihood per scored token ↓ | 2.590575 | 2.712573 | 2.615986 | 2.766394 |
| Scored PPL tokens | 8176 | 8176 | 8176 | 8176 |
| GSM8K correct / total | 23 / 32 | 23 / 32 | 24 / 32 | 23 / 32 |
| GSM8K subset accuracy | 71.875% | 71.875% | 75.000% | 71.875% |
| GSM8K outputs hitting the 256-token limit | 12 | 11 | 12 | 9 |

MXFP8 activation PPL is 9.21% lower than normal MXFP4 on this fixed subset.
Its GSM8K result differs by one answer (+3.125 percentage points); this small,
generation-limited sample does not establish a general accuracy improvement.

FWHT+MXFP4 PPL is 5.53% higher than normal MXFP4 on this subset. Both score
23/32 on GSM8K, but their extracted final answers agree on 25/32 questions;
equal aggregate scores do not establish accuracy equivalence.

The GSM8K sample is small, not random, and includes truncated answers. These
are preliminary subset results, not full benchmark scores. No BF16 accuracy
reference or full benchmark was run.

All four full-model configurations completed six qualitative prompts with
finite generated-token log probabilities.

All four full-model configurations produced these shared responses:

| Prompt/task | Observed response |
| --- | --- |
| Capital of France | The capital of France is Paris. |
| 17 × 23 | 17 * 23 = 391 |
| Translate “Machine learning helps computers learn from data.” into Chinese | 机器学习帮助计算机从数据中学习。 |

The FWHT response to the Chinese sky-color question was:

> 白天的天空呈现蓝色是因为阳光中的短波长蓝光在大气中被散射得更多。这种散射现象被称为瑞利散射，使得蓝色光线从各个方向传播到我们的眼睛。

The previous 12-layer checkpoint produced incoherent text. It is a truncated
loader/kernel smoke model, **not an accuracy reference**. Finite logprobs and
successful execution of that checkpoint were never sufficient for accuracy
acceptance. Complete-model generation now produces coherent output, but this
does not isolate every cause of the earlier behavior or prove a terminal
encoding issue.

### 7. Known limitations and unsupported configurations

- The native XPU W4A16 reference attempt was rejected by the installed
  `XPUExperts` implementation because it supports Xe2/Xe3, not CRI. Architecture
  checks were not bypassed. The successful INT4 run uses ARK WNA16.
- The default native INC MXFP4 `auto` backend was not benchmarked. The normal
  baseline in these tables is explicitly **ARK `ark_mxfp4`**, not `auto`.
- Triton attention was selected because the installed XPU FlashAttention wheel
  rejects CRI. The MoE GEMMs still use ARK CRI BDPAS.
- ARK grouped routing metadata requires host synchronization: eager execution
  is required and graph capture is unsupported.
- Optional static routing caches were disabled because native device writes do
  not increment the mutation counter those caches use.
- TP=1 only was validated. TP>1, expert parallelism, production serving load,
  long-context behavior, and full benchmark accuracy were not validated.
- INT4 is an independent accuracy reference, not a MoE-only accuracy ablation:
  its attention projections are also INT4, unlike those in the MXFP4 model.
- The FWHT path does not accept a pre-rotated checkpoint format; it transforms
  and requantizes expert weights at loading.
- No kernel-only performance comparison, matched-input TTFT/TPOT measurement,
  or runtime profiling breakdown of the MXFP8 latency gap is included. The
  staging discussion above is source analysis, not a measured attribution.

### Conclusion

The integration is exercised on real CRI hardware, including successful native
kernel tests and complete-model MXFP8/normal/FWHT runs. It establishes a working
end-to-end calling path. The current model-level measurements show near-tied
prefill-heavy batch latency and modestly slower FWHT decode-heavy latency; a performance
win is not demonstrated in these cases. The MXFP8-activation control has lower
subset PPL than normal MXFP4 but substantially higher latency in the current
implementation. Quantitative accuracy figures reported here cover INT4 W4A16,
normal MXFP4, MXFP8 activations × MXFP4 weights and FWHT+MXFP4; they are not full
benchmarks.

were assisted by GitHub Copilot; human review is required before submission.
